clue.text: Bar put in place all of a sudden

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new place, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinking bar is suddenly fitted out where it stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place' signals that the letters of BAR and PUT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrupt happens without warning, suddenly.

clue.text: A ball in court is hit with savagery

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A ball struck in a tennis court is smashed with real violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a tennis ball, but the word is only anagram fodder; 'hit' is the signal to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocious act is marked by wicked cruelty or brutality.

clue.text: What's left mother in control?

indicators.note: the word for mother sits inside the word for control

parts.note: reins are what you hold to control a horse
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A question: is what remains of the family the mother in charge?
explanation.definitionFit: Remains are the leftovers or residue of something.

clue.text: Colourful type of memory, the result of drink?

parts.note: pink is a colour
an elephant never forgets, so a long memory is called an elephant's

explanation.surface: A vivid kind of recollection brought on by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Seeing pink elephants is the traditional hallucination of the very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink elephants are the proverbial visions of someone who has drunk too much.

clue.text: Make allowance for bad group

parts.note: food gone bad has gone off
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Excusing an unruly band of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset is to counterbalance or compensate for something.

clue.text: Grass in Foreign Office gets male a release

indicators.note: the grass word goes inside the abbreviation for the ministry

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the British Foreign Office
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An informer in the Foreign Office gets a man set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like British slang for an informer, but here it is the plant REED.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom is liberty, a release from captivity.

clue.text: Advance includes credit to get clean

indicators.note: the advance word has the credit abbreviation placed within it

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages

explanation.surface: A payment in advance with credit attached settles the account.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to wash by hard rubbing.

clue.text: Attempt to keep woman in leather works

indicators.note: the attempt word holds the woman's name inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Trying to hold on to a woman working in leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where hides are made into leather.

clue.text: Enthusiastic hostility by Frenchman

parts.note: war is open hostility
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman shows eager hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is an enthusiastic, hearty one.

clue.text: I'm willing to participate in a shout of bitterness

indicators.note: taking part in something means going inside it, so these letters enter the phrase for a shout

parts.note: a cry is a shout
the apostrophe is dropped
someone willing is on, up for it

explanation.surface: Someone happy to join in a shouting match full of rancour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to participate in' puts IMON inside A CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry bitterness of feeling.

clue.text: Nerve cell registers parti-cle, taking no time

indicators.note: the time abbreviation is removed from the particle word

parts.note: a neutron is a subatomic particle

explanation.surface: A nerve cell instantly detects a particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking no' removes T (time) from NEUTRON. The hyphen in 'parti-cle' is a line break in the print.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is the basic cell of the nervous system.

clue.text: We'd sound bells when exchanging these?

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped
ding is the sound a bell makes
rings are peals of bells

explanation.surface: We would ring church bells when swapping these at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples exchange bands of gold as part of a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Such characters are comprehensible if unintelligent

parts.note: a machine has no mind of its own
readable means able to be read and understood

explanation.surface: Some letters can be understood even by the dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order: readable by something unintelligent, a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Machine-readable text is printed in a form a computer can scan.

clue.text: Shoots group of animals which might interest archaeologist

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
a herd is a group of cattle or similar animals

explanation.surface: Firing at a herd of beasts while an archaeologist looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a broken fragment of ancient pottery found on a dig.

clue.text: Face heartless man, hot and sweaty

parts.note: mug is slang for face

indicators.note: the middle letter is removed from the man word

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: Confronting a cold-hearted man who is flushed and perspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes U, the middle letter of GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggy weather is close and humid, making people sweat.

clue.text: One very taken in by brave flirt

indicators.note: the letters for one and very are enclosed by the brave word

parts.note: gallant means brave
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl utterly charmed by a bold flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam about seeking amusement, especially flirting with the opposite sex.

clue.text: Dislike having to suppress second expedition

indicators.note: holding something down inside means the second abbreviation is enclosed

parts.note: to hate is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: Hating to cut short another journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' here means speed, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its old sense is promptness or speed.

clue.text: The result of grass growing round Pennsylvania is of little worth

indicators.note: the hay word surrounds the state abbreviation

parts.note: hay is grass that has been cut and dried
Penn is a short form of Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: Grass grown around Pennsylvania is worth very little.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha'penny was the old British halfpenny coin, a byword for something nearly worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ha'penny describes something cheap and trifling, worth only a halfpenny.

clue.text: Charm of French antiquities

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from these words

explanation.surface: The appeal of old French artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to delight or bewitch.

clue.text: Band playing in foyer is an infringement of the rules

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the foyer word

parts.note: a hall is an entrance foyer

indicators.note: a band playing is in action, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band performing in the lobby breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges BAND into ANDB, which goes into HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Handball is the football offence of touching the ball with the hand.

clue.text: Dirty woman in pub

indicators.note: the woman's name sits inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
Esme is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A grubby woman in a public house.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmear is to smear over, soil or dirty.

clue.text: Breeding fish-eating birds? You can get over it

parts.note: pelicans are large fish-eating birds
crossing is breeding one strain with another

explanation.surface: Cross-breeding pelicans, which you can then climb over.
explanation.walkthrough: A PELICAN CROSSING is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls.
explanation.definitionFit: A road crossing is a place pedestrians use to get over to the other side.

clue.text: Insect form found right in volcanic eruption

indicators.note: the right abbreviation goes inside the eruption word

parts.note: lava is what a volcano pours out

explanation.surface: An insect found in a volcanic eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature grub stage of an insect.

clue.text: Number of spectators seeing wicket?

explanation.surface: Counting a crowd watching a cricket wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicket' here is not cricket but a small gate or door.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is the attendance at a sports match; a wicket is a small door or gate.

clue.text: As expected in English and not bad in French

parts.note: nor means and not
mal is French for bad

explanation.surface: Typical, expressed in English and French.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual, what one would expect.

clue.text: Insufficient legislation for ham? Quite the reverse

parts.note: under means too little
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: Weak laws for a ham actor.
explanation.walkthrough: A ham overacts; the definition asks for the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to perform with too little emphasis, the opposite of overacting.

clue.text: Making light of what's certainly a filthy place

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, certainly
a sty is a filthy pigpen

explanation.surface: Joking about a truly squalid place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making light' looks like joking, but it describes yeast making dough rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast makes bread rise and lightens the dough.

clue.text: Wit of turbulent priest

indicators.note: turbulent means in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The humour of a troublesome cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Henry II's 'turbulent priest', Thomas Becket.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit or spirit.
